hakima.name: Hakima
hakima.intro: Hakima is where network decisions are made. Each organization earns governance tokens from its contributions, and its vote carries the weight of its tokens. Every cycle has two phases: support (4 days), where proposals need 5% of tokens to qualify; then voting (3 days), where votes stay hidden until voting closes. Full participation earns your organization 30 {currency} and protects your tokens from decay.

newProposal.title: Have a proposal for the network?
newProposal.text: Each organization can submit one proposal every four months, and your next proposal is available now.

support.subtitle: Support phase · Cycle 12
support.title: Support phase is open
support.text: Each proposal needs {threshold} tokens (5% of Hakima tokens) to qualify for voting. You can support any number of proposals—support is not a vote; it only says the proposal deserves discussion.

voting.subtitle: Voting phase · Cycle 12
voting.title: Voting is open
voting.text: Four proposals qualified during support. Your vote is weighted by your token balance, and you can change it any time before voting closes.

card.carry: If it does not reach the threshold before the phase closes, the proposal is not deleted—it carries into future cycles with its existing support.

hakima.hiddenVotes: Votes stay hidden until voting closes. Nobody can see the live result. This keeps later votes independent. The number on each proposal is its support-phase total, not the vote result.

small-business-cap.title: Raise the monthly service cap for small organizations
small-business-cap.description: Organizations with fewer than five team members exhaust their monthly cap early. This raises the minimum from 80 per member to a fixed 400 {currency}.

shorter-decay.description: Shahamham currently begins decaying after a full year. This proposal shortens it to ten months so surplus circulates faster.

form.subtitle: Submit a proposal · from Mishkat Organization
form.availableNote: Each organization can submit one proposal every four months. Your last proposal was May 12.
form.qualificationNote: (5% of all Hakima tokens)—proposals below this threshold carry into future cycles.
form.title: Proposal
form.intro: Write as if explaining the proposal to an organization without context. Clarity and numbers matter more than length.
form.titlePlaceholder: One clear sentence—for example: raise the monthly service cap for small organizations
form.thresholdHint: Approval threshold for {category}: {amount} tokens ({percent}% of Hakima tokens).
form.proposalPlaceholder: What exactly should change? Write it as it should be implemented.
form.reasonPlaceholder: What problem does this solve, and what happens without it?
form.impactPlaceholder: Who will be affected, how, and are there possible negative effects?
form.impactHint: Organizations read this first when deciding whether to support.
form.upload: Drag files here or click to upload
form.uploadHint: Data, analysis, or examples · PDF or XLSX · up to 5 files
form.after: After submission: the proposal enters support at the start of the next cycle. You may edit or withdraw it during support, but its wording locks once voting begins.

validation.title: Enter a proposal title.
validation.proposalMin: The proposal must be at least 20 characters.
validation.reason: Explain why the proposal is needed.

detail.proposalText: Organizations with fewer than five team members exhaust their cap in the first half of the month and then stop exchanging until the next month. This adds a fixed 400 {currency} minimum instead of only 80 per member.
detail.whyText: The current cap ties exchange capacity to team size rather than need or activity. A three-person organization may be more active than a ten-person one, but its cap is 240 instead of 800.
impactItems: 7 of 19 organizations receive a higher cap
Expected monthly exchange growth of 12% to 18%
No effect on larger organizations already above the minimum
Limited network balance pressure because the cap resets monthly
detail.commentPlaceholder: Share your view before voting closes…
detail.voteState: You voted {choice} on September 6—you can change it until voting closes.
detail.voteChanged: You changed your vote to {choice}—you can change it until voting closes.
detail.hidden: Votes stay hidden until voting closes. The number above is support from the support phase, not the voting result.

comments.author: Sound and Vision
comments.text: The proposal makes sense, but 400 may be high as a starting point. Could we test 300 for one cycle first?

comments.author: Halqa
comments.text: We considered 300, but three affected organizations already have a cap of 240, so it would not solve the problem. The second attachment has the figures.

comments.author: Milha
comments.text: We are one of the affected organizations. We will vote rather than abstain; transparency matters more here.

comments.author: Daw
comments.text: How often will this minimum be reviewed? It could become outdated after a year.
